etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English ofspring, from Old English ofspring (“offspring, descendants, posterity”), equivalent to off- +‎ spring. Compare Icelandic afspringur (“offspring”). More at off, spring.

definitions.definition: A person's daughter or son; a person's child.
Any of a person's descendants, including of further generations.
An animal or plant's progeny or young.

quote.citation: 2013 May-June, Katrina G. Claw, “Rapid Evolution in Eggs and Sperm”, in American Scientist, volume 101, number 3:
quote.text: In plants, the ability to recognize self from nonself plays an important role in fertilization, because self-fertilization will result in less diverse offspring than fertilization with pollen from another individual.

definitions.definition: (figuratively) Anything produced; the result of an entity's efforts.
(computing) A process launched by another process.
